project_kinds.label: Generic software project
project_kinds.description: A software project without a more specific initial archetype.

project_kinds.label: Command-line tool
project_kinds.description: A bounded tool whose primary interface is a command line.

project_kinds.label: Desktop application
project_kinds.description: An interactive local application with durable user state.

project_kinds.label: Web service
project_kinds.description: A network service with explicit API and persistence boundaries.

project_kinds.label: Agent runtime
project_kinds.description: A model-driven system with tools, loops, workers, and approval boundaries.

failure_patterns.title: Scope expands before the first validated slice
failure_patterns.description: Related ideas are promoted into the active project before the smallest end-to-end path is proven.
failure_patterns.response: Freeze the final goal, select one vertical slice, and defer unrelated candidates.

failure_patterns.title: Documentation and implementation diverge
failure_patterns.description: The declared interface or state model changes without generated surfaces and tests changing with it.
failure_patterns.response: Bind contract, implementation, generated artifacts, and acceptance tests in one change.

failure_patterns.title: Distinct state identities collapse into one field
failure_patterns.description: Project, session, task, runtime, or currentness coordinates overwrite one another.
failure_patterns.response: Separate identity keys and define which operation may advance each state.

failure_patterns.title: Readiness is claimed before evidence exists
failure_patterns.description: Presence of source, configuration, or historical status is treated as a current successful run.
failure_patterns.response: Report observed references separately and retain UNKNOWN until current evidence exists.

failure_patterns.title: A new schema strands existing installations
failure_patterns.description: Validation requires new fields but the update path cannot create or migrate them safely.
signals: update passes writes then fails validation
failure_patterns.response: Ship compatibility detection and an idempotent migration before enforcing the new schema.

failure_patterns.title: Untrusted project code executes during inspection
failure_patterns.description: Review data is allowed to influence host policy or execute without an isolated boundary.
failure_patterns.response: Default to static review and require an attested disposable sandbox for execution.

failure_patterns.title: Automated work has no reliable stop condition
failure_patterns.description: A loop continues because completion depends only on an agent claim.
failure_patterns.response: Define measurable success, retry, abort, budget, and independent evaluation conditions.

routes.title: Validated software foundation
routes.description: Create the smallest observable path from goal to a tested, releasable slice.

steps.title: Fix the target state
steps.purpose: State the user-visible outcome, exclusions, and acceptance evidence.
steps.exit_evidence: A bounded goal contract with measurable completion.

steps.title: Choose the smallest architecture
steps.purpose: Select only the components required for one end-to-end path.
steps.exit_evidence: A dependency map and explicit deferred list.

steps.title: Build one vertical slice
steps.purpose: Connect input, core behavior, state, and output without placeholder claims.
steps.exit_evidence: One runnable path produces the expected output.

steps.title: Bind validation to the contract
steps.purpose: Test behavior and generated or installed surfaces that users will consume.
steps.exit_evidence: Focused automated checks pass against the actual artifact.

steps.title: Create a reproducible baseline
steps.purpose: Record source identity, build inputs, result, and known limits.
steps.exit_evidence: Another clean environment can reproduce the validated slice.

routes.title: Durable desktop application state
routes.description: Separate interactive UI state from durable domain state and background work.

steps.title: Define domain state outside the UI
steps.purpose: Give durable facts stable identities independent of windows and widgets.
steps.exit_evidence: State transitions can be tested without opening the UI.

steps.title: Project state into the UI
steps.purpose: Make views consumers of observable state rather than owners of it.
steps.exit_evidence: UI refresh does not mutate unrelated domain state.

steps.title: Bound background work
steps.purpose: Define ownership, retry, cancellation, and stale-result behavior.
steps.exit_evidence: Background operations have deterministic completion and cancellation tests.

steps.title: Prove persistence and recovery
steps.purpose: Test restart, migration, partial write, and corrupted input behavior.
steps.exit_evidence: A clean restart restores only validated durable state.

steps.title: Add operational observation
steps.purpose: Expose actionable health and event evidence without flooding file logs.
steps.exit_evidence: Failures can be diagnosed from bounded current evidence.

routes.title: Explicit service and API boundary
routes.description: Stabilize a network service around contracts, persistence, and operational evidence.

steps.title: Define the external contract
steps.purpose: Fix request, response, error, idempotency, and compatibility behavior.
steps.exit_evidence: Contract tests describe every supported outcome.

steps.title: Define persistence ownership
steps.purpose: Separate durable records, caches, queues, and derived state.
steps.exit_evidence: Every stored field has an owner and migration policy.

steps.title: Complete one request path
steps.purpose: Prove one real request through validation, state change, and response.
steps.exit_evidence: Integration test passes against the actual service boundary.

steps.title: Make failure behavior explicit
steps.purpose: Test timeout, retry, duplicate, dependency failure, and partial completion.
steps.exit_evidence: Failure responses and side effects are deterministic.

steps.title: Deploy and observe
steps.purpose: Prove startup, health, migration, rollback, and bounded telemetry.
steps.exit_evidence: A clean deployment and rollback are reproducible.

routes.title: Governed agent execution
routes.description: Separate model context, work graphs, host capability, approval, and evidence.

steps.title: Define context coordinates
steps.purpose: Separate project state, session state, task state, and executable runtime identity.
steps.exit_evidence: No identity can silently create another identity's currentness.

steps.title: Bind host capabilities
steps.purpose: Distinguish observation, proposal, sandboxed execution, and source mutation.
steps.exit_evidence: Every tool call has a source-backed capability decision.

steps.title: Create a bounded work graph
steps.purpose: Define roles, inputs, outputs, joins, retries, budgets, and stop conditions.
steps.exit_evidence: Workers cannot broaden or recursively delegate beyond allocation.

steps.title: Separate approval from evidence
steps.purpose: Ensure selection, assignment, execution, result, and adoption remain distinct.
steps.exit_evidence: A result cannot mutate source or current state without the required later gate.

steps.title: Validate hostile and interrupted paths
steps.purpose: Test untrusted instructions, stale results, crashes, replay, and partial side effects.
steps.exit_evidence: Unsafe or uncertain outcomes stop with explicit bounded states.

pivot_rules.trigger: The final goal or a defining constraint changes.
pivot_rules.procedure: Compare historical project states against the new target, rank reusable assets and transition cost, and propose the best prior state as a new branch basis.
pivot_rules.invariant: Preserve the abandoned path and its Evidence; do not rewrite history or move Current Anchor from a proposal alone.

pivot_rules.trigger: A required dependency remains unavailable or invalidates the selected route.
pivot_rules.procedure: Identify the earliest step that assumed the dependency and generate substitution, isolation, and deferment candidates.
pivot_rules.invariant: Unknown dependency behavior remains UNKNOWN and is not replaced by optimistic assumptions.

pivot_rules.trigger: Observed output fails the adopted acceptance evidence.
pivot_rules.procedure: Return to the latest state whose inputs and invariants remain valid, retain the failure as Evidence, and propose a corrected route.
pivot_rules.invariant: A failed result cannot be promoted to completion or used as a verified future pattern.
